Dragonite Multiscale+Lum as late-game DD sweeper. Watch for their Mimikyu outspeeding Garchomp (162 vs 169—mine is faster at max). Expect their Garchomp mirror; Yache helps.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Mirror match. Bring garchomp, gholdengo, dragonite? Gholdengo counters toxapex/mimikyu-ish. Garchomp leads strong. Bring garchomp, gholdengo, toxapex? Dragonite with multiscale + lum is good. I'll bring garchomp, gholdengo, dragonite.

decisions.thought: Mirror match. My Garchomp (169 Spe, Yache) vs their Gholdengo lead. EQ is super effective and I outspeed; two EQs likely KO (Gholdengo ~162-194 HP, may have Leftovers). Plan: EQ now; if they stay in, EQ again. If they switch to Dragonite/Mimikyu, reassess. Gholdengo walls Toxapex; Dragonite is my late-game DD sweeper.

Their Gholdengo fainted turn 1 to EQ. Their Dragonite at full HP (Multiscale halves first hit). My Garchomp outspeeds (169 vs ≤145). Plan: Stone Edge now—Multiscale halves it but still ~50%. If they Dragon Dance, they outspeed next turn; consider switching to my Gholdengo (resists EQ, immune to Dragon Claw? no—Dragon Claw neutral) or finish with priority later. Their third pick likely Garchomp or Rotom-Wash.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Dragonite at full HP with Multiscale. Stone Edge ~halved by Multiscale, still big damage. But they might DD. I outspeed. Stone Edge 100 BP super effective, halved by multiscale ~ still ~50%+. If they DD, they outspeed next turn. Better: Stone Edge now; if they DD, they're at ~50%, then EQ/Stone Edge again? They'd outspeed and Dragon Claw hurts. Alternatively SD then attack. Stone Edge is fine.

decisions.thought: Their Dragonite at 24%, my Garchomp at 9 HP. I outspeed. Stone Edge or Scaleshot both KO if they hit; Stone Edge 80% acc, Scaleshot ~90% per hit needing 2 hits. If I miss, their Dragon Claw KOs me. Their last Pokémon is unknown (Garchomp/Rotom/Mimikyu/Pex). My Dragonite (full, Multiscale, Lum) and Gholdengo (full) are healthy for endgame.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Stone Edge again; even if miss risk, Dragonite at 24%, Stone Edge kills. If miss, they KO me. Scaleshot also super effective, 90% acc, 2 hits at 25 BP each... 2 hits ~50-60 BP super effective vs 24% — likely kills. Scaleshot safer accuracy but multi-hit variance. Stone Edge 80% vs Scaleshot 90% (needs 2 hits, likely). Scaleshot: 25 BP ×2 hits ×1.5? No STAB. 2 hits = 50 BP SE ≈ 100 BP neutral, damage ~30-36% of max? Dragonite at 24% — likely KO with 2 hits. Scaleshot 90% accuracy overall per hit... each hit 90%. Chance of 2+ hits landing ~ decent. Stone Edge simpler: 80% kill. Scaleshot: P(≥2 hits land) = 0.81×... actually each hit checks accuracy. P(2 hits land)≈0.81, plus 3+ hits. Roughly ~85%. Similar. Go Stone Edge.

decisions.hidden_reasoning: Their Dragonite at 12%, my Garchomp fainted. Send Gholdengo—Make It Rain KOs Dragonite; resists Extreme Speed.

decisions.thought: Their Dragonite at 12%, my Gholdengo active at full HP. Make It Rain KOs it easily (Steel vs Dragon/Flying neutral, 203 SpA vs 120 SpD). Their Garchomp is at full HP and likely outspeeds my Gholdengo (104 vs up to 169); Earthquake would KO my 26% Gholdengo. Switch to full-HP Dragonite: immune to EQ, Multiscale softens Stone Edge/Dragon Claw. Then Dragon Dance and sweep with EQ/Dragon Claw/Extreme Speed. Keep Gholdengo in back for emergencies.

EQ vs Gholdengo: 182 Atk, 120 BP, Steel/Ghost weak to Ground, ~180 damage — OHKO territory. So stay in is risky. Switch to Dragonite (Multiscale, immune to EQ) is best.
